attempted_claim: Let F be a totally real field and let ρ:G_F→GL₂(Q̄₂) be continuous and unramified outside finitely many places. Fix a regular algebraic weight (k,w) in Allen's sense, with k_τ≥2 and w=k_τ+2w_τ independent of τ, and assume detρ=φε₂^(w−1) for a finite-order character φ. Assume that ρ is totally odd and nearly ordinary of weight (k,w) at every v∣2, that ρ̄ is absolutely irreducible and solvable, and that there is a 2-nearly ordinary regular algebraic cuspidal Hilbert-modular representation π₀ with ρ̄_{π₀}≅ρ̄. If L/F is the quadratic extension for which ρ̄∣G_L is abelian, must ρ be modular without assuming that, when L/F is CM, some place v∣2 is nonsplit in L?
decisive_failure: The investigation was bounded by a one-hour pass with two literature-retrieval calls, both spent on Allen's paper and one CM-field lifting paper. No new deformation-ring computation at 2 and no search for an actual non-modular representation were attempted, since both were judged out of reach within the pass once the three concrete routes were blocked. The blocked verdict rests on close reading of Allen's published proof plus elementary local arguments, not on a complete survey of all post-2014 modularity lifting literature.
